text_blocks.snippet: While many cancers are treatable and even curable, some, particularly those diagnosed at advanced stages or certain specific types, are considered incurable. Examples include metastatic melanoma, pancreatic cancer, and some cases of lung cancer, where the cancer has spread significantly. While treatment can extend life and improve quality of life, a complete cure is often not achievable.

list.title: Advanced Ovarian Cancer:

list.title: Myeloma:

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to remember that even in cases considered incurable, treatments can still help manage symptoms, slow the cancer's progression, and improve a person's quality of life.

related_questions.question: What is the #1 cause of death?

text_blocks.snippet: In the United States, heart disease is the #1 leading cause of death. It has been the top cause of death since 1950. Other leading causes of death include cancer, unintentional injuries, and COVID-19.
Here's a breakdown of the leading causes of death in the US:

list.snippet: Heart Disease: This encompasses various conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels.
Cancer: A group of diseases involving abnormal cell growth.
Unintentional Injuries: This includes accidents like motor vehicle crashes, falls, and poisonings.
COVID-19: While a significant cause of death during the pandemic, its rank has decreased in recent years.
Stroke: Also known as cerebrovascular diseases, these are conditions that affect blood supply to the brain.
Chronic Lower Respiratory Diseases: These include conditions like COPD and chronic bronchitis.
Alzheimer's Disease: A progressive brain disorder that affects memory and other cognitive functions.
Diabetes: A disease where the body doesn't produce enough insulin or can't use insulin properly.
Influenza and Pneumonia: Respiratory illnesses that can be serious, especially for vulnerable populations.
Nephritis, Nephrotic Syndrome, and Nephrosis: These are kidney diseases.
